# Retained field, avatar and effect projection

This local continuation consumes [FieldDisplays](field-wrapper-state.md), the
[World sibling owner](world-layer-display-reference.md), and the
[qualified pickup clocks](pickup-clock-reference.md). It follows merged PR149;
it is not part of that delivered batch and has not yet been published.

"'`GameRenderer` keeps World at stage(275,225). Main shake remains a separate
ancestor; user zoom remains a separate presentation scale. Field background,
actor, life and tutorial poses come from their actual retained instances. Bullet,
top-effect and highlight poses come from their World siblings. The avatar uses
its own retained pose. The player'"'s simulation coordinates are inputs to avatar
artwork, not a second camera translation. Drawing does not move or reconstruct
any source instance.

The original Point adapter uses float32 coefficients and integer twips. Root and
nested-bottom composition remain distinct. This does not turn the entire Pixi
scene into a complete Flash display tree: field masks, all retained effect/native
child poses and exact width/hit queries remain separate work.

## Original numeric oracle

The [distinct original probe](world-layer-original-reference.md) freezes90
snapshots using builtin ByteArray binary words. Original Setup, TankData._-Tr,
DeathAnimPart2 and119 synchronous ShrinkBubblefield calls actually execute.
Finish, next construction and detach controls retain their declared glue limits.
The parent consumes these independently measured values; no native helper
creates expected numbers.

"'`tests/world-layer-original.test.ts` checks cached getters, effective coefficients,
translations and original Points for root, bottom, top, bullet, highlight and
avatar at0,1,2,51,119. Separate controls check fractional Main ancestry and the
finish transform prefix without a120th shrink. Six cases make520 assertions.
They do not assert equivalence to the detached Ruffle concatenatedMatrix API,
which the original probe records as disagreeing with its localToGlobal API.

The browser collapse test uses original frozen avatar and bottom/top Point
values, retaining zoom as a separate0.75 presentation scale. Shot assertions
also check owner-to-painter projection. This replaces contradictory linear
avatar and uniformly derived layer expectations. It is a finite geometry and
paint check, not ordinary collapse scheduling, pixel equality or Adobe proof.

## Physical effect ownership

`projectEffects` visits actual registered-engine children, rather than the
completion record'"'s context or FieldRuntime compatibility effect arrays. A next
request can still be physically attached to the outgoing registered layer.
Native and mock views retain actual Effect objects, independent of gameplay UID.
Reparenting preserves the view and addChild order. Actual lower117 nesting
inherits root/under-effects alpha; top and screen remain independent siblings.

The artificial "'`effect-ownership` gallery creates a next-context request, two
same-UID objects and a physical reparent. Both asset modes must paint the
outgoing-position effect, retain separate objects and preserve reparent order.
These operations exercise actual engine and production-renderer methods; they
are not an ordinary encounter reachability claim.

The preceding actual CombatEffectsView from`f6d9ee7` is replayed separately with
the same gallery/projection/assertions, restored in a finally block. This is a
bounded prior-view regression control; it does not claim to replay the old
GameRenderer'"'s context routing or a whole historical build. Ignored artifacts
record the exact source/restoration digests and failures.

## Explicit artificial layouts

Several galleries directly replace player coordinates, transit offsets, wave
scale or tutorial metadata. These scalar edits do not represent Flash display
setters. "'`tools/fixtures/field-layout.ts` explicitly supplies their omitted source
move/follow/setup operations; tutorial substitutions explicitly call the stopped
clip selector. These adapters are invoked at artificial edits, never from
production drawing or automatic array discovery. The actor reparent expectation
remains415; its omitted display move is supplied instead of changing the
assertion. Superseded wrapper poses are left retained during subsequent steps.

## Validation and boundaries

Exact commands, source/build identities, browser reports, negative controls and
cleanup are retained under ignored`test-results/retained-renderer/`. The final
validation record is added after the repaired fixtures and restored production
sources pass together.

No artwork entropy or native-effect playback scheduler was qualified here.
Actual effect poses still use the existing per-view entropy adapter. Bullet
render identity remains its preceding UID-based implementation. Complete field
shape/mask/order composition, dynamic Script width/hit geometry, ordinary earned
boss/win progression, global RNG/event equality, compiled Ruffle revision and
Adobe/pixel/audio/full-game parity remain unproved. No provider settings,
deployment retry, protected branch or research source was changed.
EOF

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.
